body:
Marius meets a new arrival’s questions with patient explanations, then cautions her against letting a noble purpose change her beyond recognition. His precision leaves room for someone else’s perspective.

A conversation between the stalls

Marius is browsing rings and pendants when he notices Kiralyn. He introduces himself and asks how long she has been in Pristinia. He says he has been here for nearly fifteen months, qualifying even his sense of time. When she has questions, he offers to answer them as well as he can.

The first answers are ordinary ones. He describes the cotton and wool in his clothing and cleans it with a small spell. Kiralyn is looking for garments that protect without making heat harder to bear. Marius points her toward the mundane shops and the seamstresses who can repair damaged clothes. His explanation of the war comes as his understanding, not privileged knowledge of every arrival’s purpose.

Explaining how other people’s work joins up

He distinguishes gathering useful materials from taking potent parts from monsters, then connects both to craft. Pristinia’s walls are his example of people turning supplies into a public project. The Adventurer Emporium interests him too. He remembers an earlier keeper and wants an item whose making may be difficult; his conversation does not establish that it is made.

Marius also explains the islands through what he has heard of Scribonia’s discoveries: places separated in ways that make travel unusually demanding. He qualifies what he knows and asks about Kiralyn’s familiarity with magic before going further. His account is useful to a newcomer, while remaining an account given in conversation.

When she asks about disorganization, he says regimental discipline has not found much support among adventurers. He suggests finding like-minded people or organizing the work herself. Walls, temples and the bathhouse give him concrete examples of what effort has already changed.

A book she should keep writing

His warning is quieter than his explanation. Kiralyn’s reasons for fighting may be good, he says, but someone could twist them until her earlier self would no longer recognize her. He relates that concern to his own homeland, without supplying its full history.

Kiralyn offers him her writing. Marius reads it honestly and returns it: the work is hers, and her views may change as she stays longer. He finds value in learning how another person sees events. He also knows why a damaged coat matters. The possessions people brought through the Gate can be their remaining connection to home.

He ends with practical advice again: caution in the alpine country and a suggestion to ask Herb about edible plants. No completed editing partnership or expedition follows. For this meeting, he has made the new place easier to ask about.
